newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen higher with bonds on prices data. b
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen higher with bonds on prices data. b

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to open higher with bonds on Friday after August consumer prices and retail sales pointed to a moderately growing economy with tame inflation, analysts said.

"What it does is confirms the non-inflationary trend we saw in yesterday's PPI and truly calls into question whether the Fed needs to take any action September 24," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.
"It would appear we have the best of both possible worlds -- good modest economic growth and the absence of inflationary pressures."
Before the data was released, analysts said benign figures could spark a rally that would send the Dow Jones Industrial Average to new highs.
The Dow settled on Thursday at 5,772, up 17 and just shy of May 22's record closing high of 5,778.
